for the financial year 2025-26 Dear Sir/Madam, This is to inform that the 18th Annual General Meeting (“AGM”) of the Company is scheduled to be held on Monday, September 28, 2026 at 11:00 A.M. (IST) through Video Conferencing (“VC”)/ Other Audio Visual Means (“OAVM”) in compliance with the applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 and the rules made thereunder read with General Circular No. 03/2025 dated September 22, 2025, issued by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (“MCA”), the Securities and Exchange Board of India (“SEBI”) (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“SEBI Listing Regulations”) and other applicable circulars issued in this regard by MCA and SEBI (collectively referred to as “Circulars”). Pursuant to Regulation 30 & 34 of the SEBI Listing Regulations, we are enclosing herewith the following: 1. Notice convening 18th Annual General Meeting of the Company (“Notice”) 2. Integrated Annual Report of the Company for the financial year ended March 31, 2026 (“Annual Report”) In accordance with the aforesaid circulars, the Notice convening the 18th AGM and the Annual Report are being sent through electronic mode to all the members of the Company whose names appear in the register of members / list of beneficial owners as on Friday, August 28, 2026 and whose e-mail addresses are registered with the Company/ registrar and share transfer agent (“RTA”)/ Depositories/Depository Participant (“DPs”). The Notice convening the AGM along with the Annual Report is also uploaded on the Company’s website at https://www.pbfintech.in/investor-relations/ and on the website of Registrar and Transfer Agent of the Company i.e. MUFG Intime India Private Limited (‘MUFG’) at https://instavote.linkintime.co.in.

The Company has appointed MUFG Intime India Private Limited (‘MUFG’) as the e-voting Agency and has decided to provide the facility to vote by electronic means (remote e-voting as well as e- voting at the AGM) on all resolutions (as set out in the notice) to those members, who will hold share(s) either in physical or in electronic form as on Monday, September 21, 2026 (“Cut-off date”). The remote e-voting shall commence on Friday, September 25, 2026 at 09:00 A.M. (IST) and ends on Sunday, September 27, 2026 at 05:00 P.M. (IST).
The above said disclosure will also be hosted on the website of the Company at www.pbfintech.in. You are requested to kindly take the same in your records. Thanking you, Yours faithfully, For PB Fintech Limited ______________ (Bhasker Joshi) Company Secretary and Compliance Officer Encl.: A/a

NOTICE

NOTICE
NOTICE is hereby given that the 18th Annual General Meeting (AGM) of the members of PB Fintech Limited (“the Company”) will be held on Monday, September 28, 2026 at 11:00 AM (IST) through Video Conferencing (VC) / Other Audio Visual Means (OAVM) organized by the Company, to transact the following businesses. The venue of the meeting shall be deemed to be the Registered Office of the Company at Plot No. 119, Sector-44, Gurugram- 122001, Haryana.
ORDINARY BUSINESS(ES):
1. To receive, consider and adopt the Audited Standalone Financial Statements and Audited Consolidated Financial Statements of the Company for the Financial Year ended March 31, 2026, together with the Reports of the Board of Directors and the Auditors thereon and, in this regard, to consider and if thought fit, to pass, with or without modification(s), the following resolution as an Ordinary Resolution:
“RESOLVED THAT the audited standalone and consolidated Financial Statements of the Company together with the report of the Board of Directors and the Auditors’ thereon for the Financial Year ended March 31, 2026, as circulated to the Members, be and are hereby considered and adopted.”

“RESOLVED THAT the audited standalone and consolidated Financial Statements of the Company together with the report of the Board of Directors and the Auditors’ thereon for the Financial Year ended March 31, 2026, as circulated to the Members, be and are hereby considered and adopted.”
2. To re-appoint Ms. Kitty Agarwal (DIN: 07624308) as a Non-Executive Nominee Director, who retires by rotation and being eligible, offers herself for re-appointment and, in this regard, to consider and if thought fit, to pass, with or without modification(s), the following resolution as an Ordinary Resolution:
“RESOLVED THAT in accordance with the provisions of Section 152 and other applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013, Ms. Kitty Agarwal (DIN: 07624308), Non-Executive Nominee Director who retires by rotation at this meeting, be and is hereby re-appointed as the Non-Executive Nominee Director of the Company liable to retire by rotation.”

1. The Register of Members and Share Transfer Books of the Company will remain closed from Tuesday, September 22, 2026, to Monday, September 28, 2026 (both days inclusive) for the purpose of 18th Annual General Meeting (‘AGM’).
2. Pursuant to General Circular Nos. 09/2024 dated September 19, 2024, 03/2025 dated September 22, 2025 issued by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (“MCA”), and Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-2/P/ CIR/2024/133 dated October 3, 2024 issued by SEBI read with other relevant circulars, notifications, guidelines issued by MCA and SEBI (including any amendment(s), statutory modification(s) or re-enactment(s) thereof for the time being in force) (collectively referred to as “Circulars”), companies are allowed to convene their AGM through VC or OAVM, without the physical presence of members at a common venue. Accordingly, in compliance with the aforesaid Circulars, AGM of the Company is being held through VC/ OAVM. The members are requested to attend and participate in the AGM through VC/ OAVM.
13. Members attending the AGM through VC/ OAVM shall be counted for the purpose of reckoning the quorum under Section 103 of the Act.

13. Members attending the AGM through VC/ OAVM shall be counted for the purpose of reckoning the quorum under Section 103 of the Act.
14. Voting rights of members shall be in proportion to the paid-up equity share capital of the Company held by them, as on the Cut-off date i.e. Monday, September 21, 2026. In the case of joint holders, the member whose name appears as the first holder in the order of the names as per the register of members of the Company/ records of the depository as on cut-off date will be entitled to vote at the meeting.
3. The Circulars have dispensed with the requirement of sending the physical copies of the AGM Notice and Annual Report to the shareholders. Accordingly, this Notice, along with the Annual Report for the financial year ended March 31, 2026 (“Annual Report for F.Y. 2025-26”), is being sent only through electronic mode to those shareholders whose e-mail addresses are registered with the Company/ registrar and share transfer agent (“RTA”)/ depositories/ depository participants (“DP”) as on August 28, 2026. Additionally, as per SEBI Listing Regulations, the Company is also sending a letter to shareholders whose e-mail addresses are not registered with Company/ RTA/ depositories/ DP providing the weblink, including the exact path of Company’s website where the complete details of the Notice and Annual Report for F.Y. 2025-26, is available.

A person who is not a member on the Cut-off date should treat this Notice for information purposes only.

An Indian family should be able to understand the insurance it buys. Eighteen years ago, that simple idea contrasted with how the market worked. Insurance was sold, not chosen, and the cover a household needed the most was the cover it understood least. Policybazaar was built to change that, through honest comparison and plain information. Policybazaar simplifies protection and Paisabazaar opens access to credit. PB Partners equips advisors to serve Bharat, PB UAE carries our model across borders. Around this core, newer verticals extend the ecosystem further. Pensionbazaar aims to solve for retirement solutions, PB Wheels aims to act as one-stop platform for the motor ownership journey, the Reinsurance broking business acts as an intermediary between insurers and reinsurers, Account aggregation (PB Money) gives customers a single, consolidated view of their finances across institutions.
Eventually, the platform became only part of the story. Customers who came to compare stayed for claims support. Families who bought term cover returned for goal-based plans. Borrowers who checked their score came back to transact. The relationship did not end at the transaction. More often, that was where it began.

PB Fintech is the parent company of two of India's leading digital marketplaces for insurance and credit, Policybazaar and Paisabazaar. We were built around a single, durable purpose: to help India's middle class withstand the three financial shocks that can undo a lifetime of saving, namely death, disease and disability. For eighteen years that purpose has guided every decision we have made, and it remains the organising idea of the business today.

We began by offering product comparisons to help customers identify the most suitable options. Over the years, we steadily deepened that experience, progressing from telephone assistance to chat, to video interactions, and eventually to in-person meetings. What began as a platform for comparisons became a holistic ecosystem of services. We first empowered customers to purchase through insurer platforms, then advanced to a single-interface payment experience, and further extended into post-purchase support – from documentation and medical check-ups to vehicle-inspection surveys, so that customers feel supported well beyond the moment of purchase.
Credit When we established Paisabazaar in 2014, our goal was to simplify the credit journey for Indian customers and bring transparency to a traditionally complex marketplace. It has since become the country's leading credit-aggregation platform, working with more than 70 lending partners and serving customers across the full spectrum, from Super-Prime and Prime to Sub-Prime and New-to-Credit, as well as SMEs seeking growth capital. This inclusivity underscores our commitment to bridging financial access gaps across the credit spectrum.

The Asset Light Model We operate an asset-light, digital-first model. We do not underwrite insurance or carry credit risk on our own books. Instead, we sit between consumers and the institutions that serve them – insurers, banks and non-bank lenders – and we earn our place by making complex financial decisions simpler, more transparent and more honest. Our role is discovery, advise and service: helping a consumer understand what they need, compare options without bias, transact with confidence, and get help when it matters the most, i.e. Claims.

Deepening Distribution into Bharat
India’s digital evolution has changed how customers discover, evaluate and buy insurance, however a large part of India particularly in small cities still need human assistance, vernacular medium and reassurance. Insurance is an infrequent, complex and consequential purchase. Customers may begin online, yet many still want to speak with someone they know before committing.
PB Partners was launched in 2021, to address these critical gaps in insurance distribution. The idea was rooted in expanding insurance accessibility deep across Bharat. Across Bharat, independent insurance sellers (Point of Sales Persons) already generate demand through their own offline relationships and local networks. What PB Partners provides is the institutional capability that an individual independent insurance seller would find difficult to build alone. Through the app and website, a partner can access products from multiple insurers, research and compare options, customise quotations, upload documents, and track performance. The same platform supports the relationship after the sale through endorsements, renewals, service requests and claims assistance. This complements Policybazaar’s direct digital model by serving customers who prefer to transact through a familiar local advisor.

PB Partners empowers independent insurance sellers though a unified platform. This Product-as-a-service solutions enables POSP agents/partners to access and sell a wide range of products from multiple providers via a single app, driving cross sell opportunities, enhancing coverage and fueling business growth through a scalable distribution model.

How to read our attrition

How to read our attrition
Most companies selling financial products by telephone outsource that work to third-party contact centres. We do not. Our advisors are permanent employees of our subsidiaries, on our own rolls, with full statutory benefits, access to internal job posting and eligibility for sales incentives. Around 90% of our workforce sits in these frontline advisory and service roles.
Hiring across Tier-2, Tier-3 and rural India We are widening access to opportunity by recruiting from emerging cities and strengthening the regional workforce. Training was adapted into multilingual formats and policies adjusted for local conditions. Creating employment in smaller towns lets people build a career without leaving home, which improves retention.
Employee voice We have formalized the measurement of employee experience. Engagement is currently read through participation rates, referral behaviour, exit conversations, Whatsapp based pulse checks, and skip-level forums; a structured, externally benchmarked engagement survey with a published score and a forward target is being introduced.

Stability of the workforce Tenure is where a people strategy is finally tested. As on 31 March 2026, 2,134 employees had been with us five years or more and 307 for ten years or more, particularly in an organisation that grew from 15,467 to 28,330 people in three years. Ten-year completers receive ESOP/LTIP, aligning tenure with ownership.
We largely hire freshers into these roles. It also means a large share of our people are at the earliest, least settled stage of their careers, still deciding what they want to do. Most of our separations therefore happen inside the first few months, frequently before an advisor completes probation and reaches full productivity.
That is why we publish two rates. Headline attrition counts every separation. Attrition (excluding attrition in first six months of employment with us) – 23% in FY25 and 25% in FY26.

MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION & ANALYSIS
Economic Overview Economic Overview
The Outlook Ahead Based on the Reserve Bank of India’s August 2026 projection, real GDP is expected to grow 6.7% in FY2027. Although this represents moderation from the high FY2026 base, growth is expected to remain well above the global rate. Union Budget 2026 –27 continues to emphasise growth, capacity creation and inclusion. Resilient household demand and moderating inflation should support protection, savings and credit. Energy prices, trade-policy changes and a slower global rate cycle remain the principal external risks to disposable incomes and financial conditions. The operating implication is to preserve underwriting and cost discipline while continuing to invest in access, advice and service.
The second material change was the GST exemption for individual life and health insurance premiums, effective 22 September 2025. It applies to new business and renewals, lowering the cost of cover and supporting acquisition and persistency. For households managing several claims on income, a lower premium can be the difference between considering protection and postponing it. The measure also aligns with ‘Insurance for All by 2047’.

Inflation and Monetary Policy Global headline inflation moderated to 4.1% in CY2025. The IMF projects it to rise to 4.7% in CY2026 before easing to 3.9% in CY2027, reflecting energy prices and geopolitical tensions. Goods inflation has softened, while energy and services remain sensitive to supply disruption and wage pressure. With inflation above target in several major economies, monetary easing is expected to remain cautious and uneven, keeping global funding conditions relatively tight.
The global economy remained resilient through CY2025 as inflation moderated, although trade and energy risks continued to shape the outlook. India’s real GDP grew 7.7% in FY2026, supported by broad-based domestic demand. Against this backdrop, insurance penetration remained 3.7% of GDP, indicating significant scope for deeper social security and formal credit.

Mortality Protection Gap Swiss Re estimates India’s mortality protection gap at 97%. This means only about 3% of the estimated protection need is insured; it is not a population-coverage statistic. The comparison remains wide even against China at 88% and the United States at 82%.
India’s low insurance intensity and uneven access to formal credit represent a significant long-term industry opportunity. Insurance penetration remained 3.7% in FY2025 and density was US$97, both well below global levels. The next phase of growth will depend on affordable, customer-centric products, trusted advice and service capable of converting financial need into sustained protection and responsible credit usage.

Term insurance is designed for this gap, yet it is poorly understood and historically unattractive to a face-to-face seller. Low price, low awareness and a high need for explanation is precisely the combination in which transparent comparison and assisted digital advice can change category economics.

PB Fintech operates through two Core Online businesses: Policybazaar and Paisabazaar, and three New Initiatives: PB Partners, PB for Business and Policybazaar.ae. Each addresses a distinct customer need, market or mode of engagement, while drawing on common capabilities across technology, data and risk intelligence, insurer and lender integrations, advisory, service and claims.

Policybazaar is the Group’s Core Online insurance marketplace in India, providing access to health, term life, savings, motor and travel products from 53 insurer partners. During FY2026, the platform served 5.8 million transacting customers. Cumulative insurance-transacting consumers reached 26.4 million, policies sold reached 67.3 million and registered consumers stood at 145.7 million as at March 2026.
The commercial logic is not diversification for its own sake. The businesses reach customers who prefer different routes to purchase for e.g. a digitally self-directed consumer, a household seeking in-person advice, an enterprise buying employee or commercial cover, or a UAE resident with cross-border needs. Sharing the underlying operating capabilities allows the Group to broaden access efficiently and use each interaction to improve future decisions.

The portfolio includes maternity and OPD benefits, two-hour hospitalisation cover and zero-waiting-period options for selected pre-existing conditions. The objective was to make cover more relevant to the way households actually use healthcare.

Credit Awareness and Progression Credit information is often technical and difficult for consumers to interpret. Paisabazaar’s credit-progression strategy therefore begins with awareness. Free-for-life credit scores, monthly updates across all four credit bureaus, AI-generated video reports and Credit Health insights translate bureau data into plain language and identify actions customers can take to strengthen their credit profile. During FY2026, customers completed 13.55 lakh credit-improvement transactions, while overall customer satisfaction increased to 91%.

Around 80% of business was generated in Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets. The platform worked with 45 insurer partners across motor, health and life insurance and maintained a diversified portfolio with a relatively high contribution from non-motor products.
Product and Pricing Innovation Pay-as-you-drive plans allow customers to select cover based on expected usage, while multi-year products reduce annual renewal requirements. Video-based inspection discounts, good-driver benefits and preferred-garage propositions use observable behaviour to improve pricing accuracy and affordability.
Importantly, growth became more broad-based. Share of small partners in total premium is continuously increasing. A growing proportion of partners also began selling across more than one product category, indicating deeper platform adoption and the development of more durable advisory practices.
Goal-based Planning Goal-based propositions connect a policy to outcomes such as education or retirement. Under Waiver of Premium variants, if the insured customer dies, the insurer funds the remaining premiums and the planned maturity benefit continues, protecting the underlying financial objective.

Service Economics Motor is a high-frequency category in which claims and renewal experience directly influence retention. Better inspection, garage coordination and post-sale visibility can reduce avoidable leakage for insurers while making the product easier for customers to use. The category also creates a regular point of re-engagement with younger households entering the broader insurance relationship.
For new-to-credit and emerging customers, understanding the score is only the first step. Paisa+, an FD-backed secured credit card launched with SBM Bank, provides a controlled entry point for establishing repayment history with limited risk exposure. Continuous monitoring and personalised insights then help customers improve their eligibility and, over time, graduate to mainstream credit. Together, these capabilities create an end-to-end pathway from understanding one’s credit position to improving it, building a formal credit record and accessing more suitable products.

STRATEGY Strategy
Opportunity

Opportunity
India's opportunity is not limited to moving existing financial transactions online. It lies in bringing more households and enterprises into formal protection and credit, improving the adequacy and suitability of the products they hold, and supporting them for longer. Rising incomes, formalisation and digital infrastructure have expanded access, but gaps remain in awareness, affordability, product understanding and continuing service.
PB Fintech's strategy is to help customers make important financial decisions with greater confidence and remain supported after the transaction. Policybazaar and Paisabazaar are the Group's Core Online businesses. PB Partners, PB for Business and Policybazaar.ae extend these capabilities into advisor-led distribution, commercial insurance and the UAE. Their shared foundation includes technology, data, partner relationships, advice, service and claims support.
For PB Fintech, this creates connected opportunities to expand participation, improve decisions and remain relevant through renewal, repayment, claims and changing financial needs. The opportunity follows a sequence: help a customer recognise a need, make a suitable product accessible, support completion and remain accountable after the transaction.

During FY26, the Group focused on protection-led growth, stronger recurring revenue and disciplined execution. Investment continued where customer participation and long-term value could increase.
3. Collaborative innovation with partners PB Fintech works with insurers, lenders and other regulated partners to develop products and journeys around needs that standard offerings do not always address. Customer feedback and operating data are combined with partner underwriting and product expertise to improve relevance, affordability and access. Recent innovations include unlimited sum insured plans, maternity benefits, more flexible payment options and solutions for women, homemakers, self-employed customers and NRIs. Collaboration also extends to documentation, product integrations and service workflows that reduce avoidable delays. The aim is to improve outcomes for customers while supporting stronger, more sustainable partner portfolios. This allows partners to expand access without weakening risk or service standards.

1. Protection-led and responsible growth The Group's priority is to help families manage the financial consequences of illness, loss of income and the death of an earning member. In insurance, this means expanding access to health and term cover, improving affordability and encouraging adequate, continuing protection. Savings recommendations reflect a customer's goals, household resources and appetite for risk. In credit, growth is balanced with suitability, repayment capacity and a practical path towards formal borrowing. Progress is assessed through first-time participation, quality of cover, policy renewals, responsible repayment and customer experience. Policies that remain in force and loans that can be repaid are stronger measures of progress than transaction volume alone.

Expanding participation in protection Large sections remain without adequate health or term cover, particularly first-time buyers, younger households, the self-employed, women, senior citizens and customers beyond major urban markets. Many households have the ability to pay but require propositions matched to irregular income, life stage, pre-existing conditions or unfamiliarity with insurance. Monthly payment options, broader health benefits and products designed around specific customer circumstances can make entry more practical. Progress also requires understandable terms, trusted advice and confidence in post-purchase support. Product co-creation, assisted journeys and service can therefore address barriers that distribution alone cannot solve.

Deepening existing customer relationships A substantial part of the opportunity lies beyond the first transaction. Insurance renewals, credit progression, repeat lending, savings and investment products, and continuing service allow relationships to develop over time. Each year of persistency adds revenue without repeating the original acquisition effort, while more frequent engagement provides better insight into changing protection, liquidity and borrowing needs. Claims assistance, renewal support and portfolio visibility can reinforce trust at the moments that determine whether a customer stays. Fixed deposits, bonds, payments and other adjacent products can extend the relationship where they solve a relevant need. The objective is lifecycle participation, not indiscriminate cross-selling.

Converting access into informed action Access does not automatically produce a sound decision. Insurance remains complex to compare, while credit reports and eligibility criteria can be difficult to interpret. Personalised explanations, suitability-led recommendations, planning tools and assisted journeys can reduce the distance between information and action. Plain-language and video explanations can make credit information more usable, while track-and-manage journeys give customers a reason to return between borrowing events. In credit, this means helping customers understand their bureau information, improve readiness, establish repayment history and progress towards suitable mainstream products. Better matching also reduces unnecessary applications and processing leakage for partners.

2. Trust through service and claims support Trust is tested when a customer needs help, particularly during the time of claim. PB Fintech supports customers with documentation, pre-authorisation, hospital coordination, claim tracking, follow-up and grievance resolution. Multilingual and on-ground teams provide assistance, while technology helps identify missing information and service delays earlier. The Group's role is to help customers understand the claims process and receive timely support, while Insurers remain responsible for evaluating and settling claims. The aim is to remove uncertainty at difficult moments, so customers are not left to coordinate among the hospital, insurer and administrator alone. Claims experience also informs product communication, advisory and service improvements. Confidence in the claims journey influences whether families buy adequate cover, renew their policies and recommend insurance to others.

4. AI, Technology and Data driven approach Technology, data and AI support customer matching, risk assessment, proposal completion, service, renewals and claims assistance. AI-generated explanations help make complex information usable; matching engines reduce irrelevant applications; risk models improve suitability; and workflow intelligence identifies incomplete proposals or potential service issues earlier. Automation improves routine execution, while advisors and service teams remain important where explanation or intervention is required.
Extending reach through complementary channels Different customer segments require different modes of engagement. PB Partners combines digital infrastructure with the trust and continuing service of local advisors, particularly in Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets. PB for Business uses employee benefits as an entry point into wider corporate and SME risk requirements, supported by claims and service workflows. Policybazaar.ae adapts the Group’s proven model to the UAE, where customers share many of the same needs as those in India. Shared technology, integrations, risk intelligence and service infrastructure allow these businesses to broaden reach without recreating the entire operating platform for every channel or market. Their progress will be judged by contribution and customer outcomes, not reach alone.
Allied Opportunities

Allied Opportunities
Regulated pathways and focused adjacencies During FY26, the Group received an NBFC-Account Aggregator licence and approval for a Payment Aggregator licence, established a Policybazaar branch in GIFT City, and advanced Pensionbazaar, PB Wheels and PB Pay. These activities remain early-stage. Their relevance lies in extending journeys the Group already serves through consent-based financial insight, lower payment friction, retirement solutions and mobility services. Progress will be assessed against customer relevance, regulatory fit, capital intensity and sustainable economics.
Reinsurance Broking Reinsurance broking can connect insurers and corporate clients with domestic and global capacity, support specialised risk placement and add fee income without placing underwriting risk on the Group's balance sheet. PB Fintech's insurance data and partner relationships can also support product design and placement insight. The opportunity will be developed with the same discipline applied to other New Initiatives.
Trust, governance and people

Trust, governance and people
Trust underpins every part of our strategy. For customers, it requires transparent information, suitability-led advice, dependable service and support when a claim or grievance arises. For partners, it requires fairness, transparency and a shared commitment to the long-term health of the ecosystem. For regulators, it requires responsible conduct, appropriate controls and timely compliance.
Our people translate these commitments into everyday decisions. We seek to attract, develop and retain professionals who combine category expertise with a strong sense of customer responsibility. An intrapreneurial culture encourages autonomy and innovation, accompanied by clear accountability for outcomes. Sharing effective practices across businesses enables the Group to learn faster while preserving the specialist capabilities required in each market.

Sustainability and Our Capitals Sustainability shapes how we allocate resources and where we invest. We work to reduce the environmental footprint of our operations and to strengthen the value we create for our people, our customers and the communities we serve. We report that value through our six capitals, and the risk framework is designed to protect each of them.
• Localisation of compliance protocols, so that KYC, AML and data sovereignty requirements meet the standards of each host regulator • A centralised risk policy engine and governance dashboard, giving executive management and the Board a consistent view • Stress-testing for new verticals such as PB Health, with particular focus on provider integration and patient data security • Partnership risk models for embedded finance and APIs, including capped arrangements with our lending partners

As PB Fintech has grown from a pioneering digital web aggregator into a diversified fintech ecosystem, our risk framework has changed with it. What began as a functional necessity has become a strategic imperative. At the heart of this evolution is our commitment to managing risk not as a constraint but as a core lever of innovation, resilience and trust. As India's financial landscape expands in complexity and scale, so does the need for robust, forward-looking oversight that is adaptive by design and unified in purpose.

ii) Defined benefits plans
For defined benefits plans in the form of gratuity, the cost of providing benefits is determined using the Projected Unit Credit method, with actuarial valuations being carried out at each balance sheet date. Re-measurement, comprising actuarial gains and losses, the effect of the changes to the asset ceiling and the return on plan asset, is reflected immediately in the balance sheet with a charge or credit recognised in other comprehensive income in the period in which they occur. Re-measurement recognised in other comprehensive income is reflected immediately in retained earnings and is not reclassified to the statement of profit and loss. Past service cost is recognised in profit and loss in the period of a plan amendment. Net interest is calculated by applying the discount rate at the beginning of the period to the net defined liability or asset.

b) National Pension Scheme (NPS)
a) Securities premium

a) Securities premium
The Company has a defined contribution plan in respect of the National Pension Scheme for eligible employees who opt for it. Contributions are made to the National Pension Scheme for such employees in accordance with the scheme rules. The contributions are made to the National Pension System Trust, a scheme regulated by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA). The obligation of the Company is limited to the amount contributed in respect of eligible employees who opt for it and it has no further contractual nor any constructive obligation. The expense recognised during the year ended March 31, 2026 towards defined contribution plan is ₹ 41 Lakhs (March 31, 2025- ₹33 Lakhs) [refer note 16]
Securities premium is used to record the premium on issue of shares. Securities premium is utilised in accordance with the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013.
b) Retained earnings
This represents surplus/(deficit) of profit and loss account and cumulative gains and losses arising on the remeasurement of defined benefits plans in accordance with Ind AS 19 that have been recognised in other comprehensive income
(iii) Post employment benefits plan obligations- Gratuity
c) Equity settled share based payment reserve

c) Equity settled share based payment reserve
The Company provides for gratuity for employees as per the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972. Employees who are in continuous service for a period of 5 years are eligible for gratuity. The amount of gratuity payable on retirement/ termination is the employees last drawn basic salary per month computed proportionately for 15 days salary multiplied for the number of years of service. The gratuity plan is a funded plan and the Company makes contribution to recognised funds in India. The Company does not fully fund the liability and maintains a target level of funding to be maintained over a period of time based on estimations of expected gratuity payments.
Equity settled share based payment reserve is used to recognise the grant date fair value of options issued to the employees of the Company and its subsidiaries under ESOP scheme.

B) Capital management
Credit risk on cash and cash equivalents and other deposits with banks is limited as the Company generally invest in deposits with banks with high credit ratings assigned by external credit rating agencies, accordingly the Company considers that the related credit risk is low. Impairment on these items are measured on the 12-month expected credit loss basis.

A company’s internal financial controls with reference to financial statements is a process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. A company’s internal financial controls with reference to financial statements include those policies and procedures that (1) pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the company; (2) provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the company are being made only in accordance with authorisations of management and directors of the company; and (3) provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorised acquisition, use, or disposition of the company’s assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements.

h. Intangible assets
Intangible assets are stated at acquisition cost, net of accumulated amortisation and accumulated impairment losses, if any. Intangible assets with indefinite useful lives or not yet available are not amortised but instead tested for impairment annually. Intangible assets with finite lives are amortised on a straight-line basis over their estimated useful lives. The amortisation period and the amortisation method are reviewed at least at each financial year end. If the expected useful life of the asset is significantly different from previous estimates, the amortisation period is changed accordingly. Gains or losses arising from the retirement or disposal of an intangible asset are determined as the difference between the net disposal proceeds and the carrying amount of the asset and recognised as income or expense in the Statement of Profit and Loss.

The Group bases its impairment calculation on detailed budgets and forecast calculations. These budgets and forecast calculations generally cover a period of five years. For longer periods, a long-term growth rate is calculated and applied to project future cash flows after the fifth year. To estimate cash flow projections beyond periods covered by the most recent budgets/forecasts, the Company extrapolates cash flow projections in the budget using a steady or declining growth rate for subsequent years, unless an increasing rate can be justified. In any case, this growth rate does not exceed the long-term average growth rate for the products, industries, or country or countries in which the entity operates, or for the market in which the asset is used.

Depreciation methods, estimated useful lives and residual value
A cash generating unit to which goodwill has been allocated is tested for impairment annually, or more frequently when there is an indication that the unit may be impaired. If the recoverable amount of the cash generating unit is less than its carrying amount, the impairment loss is allocated first to reduce the carrying amount of any goodwill allocated to the unit and then to the other assets of the unit pro rata based on the carrying amount of each asset in the unit. Any impairment loss for goodwill is recognised in the statement of profit and loss. An impairment loss recognised for goodwill is not reversed in subsequent periods.
Depreciation is recognised so as to write off the cost of assets less their residual values over the useful lives, using the straight line method. The useful lives have been determined based on technical evaluation performed by the management which in some cases are different as compared to those specified by Schedule II to the Companies Act, 2013, in order to reflect the actual usage of the assets.

An assessment is made at each reporting date to determine whether there is an indication that previously recognised impairment losses no longer exist or have decreased. If such indication exists, the Group estimates the asset’s or CGU’s recoverable amount. A previously recognised impairment loss is reversed only if there has been a change in the assumptions used to determine the asset’s or CGU’s recoverable amount since the last impairment loss was recognised. The reversal is limited so that the carrying amount of the asset does not exceed its recoverable amount, nor exceed the carrying amount that would have been determined, net of depreciation, had no impairment loss been recognised for the asset in prior years. Such reversal is recognised in the statement of profit and loss.

The assessment of reasonable certainty is only revised if a significant event or a significant change in circumstances occurs, which affects this assessment, and that is within the control of the lessee.

For the purpose of impairment testing, goodwill acquired in a business combination is allocated to the cash generating unit (CGU), which benefits from the synergies of the acquisition. Goodwill is tested for impairment at least annually. Impairment is recognised, when the carrying amount of cash generating units (CGU) including goodwill, exceeds the estimated recoverable amount of CGU.

(iii) Post employment benefits plan obligations- Gratuity

(iii) Post employment benefits plan obligations- Gratuity
Based on management assessment and the best information available, and in line with the guidance issued by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (“ICAI”), the incremental impact of these changes is not material to the consolidated financial statements of the Company for the year ended March 31, 2026.
The Group provides for gratuity to employees in the India region as per the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, and to employees in the Middle East region as governed by the United Arab Emirates Labour Laws. Under the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, employees who are in continuous service for a period of 5 years are eligible for gratuity. The amount of gratuity payable on retirement/termination is the employees last drawn basic salary per month computed proportionately for 15 days salary multiplied for the number of years of service. The India region gratuity plan is a funded plan and the Group makes contribution to recognised funds in India. The Group does not fully fund the liability and maintains a target level of funding to be maintained over a period of time based on estimations of expected gratuity payments.

The Company continues to monitor the finalisation of Central and State Rules and clarifications from the Government on other aspects of the Labour Code and would provide appropriate accounting effect subsequently on the basis of such developments as needed.

(a) Employee option plan

(a) Employee option plan
The Company instituted the Employee Stock Option Plan(s) to grant equity based incentives to eligible employees of the Company and its subsidiaries. The Company has four ESOP schemes, namely, Employee Stock Option Plan 2014 (“ESOP– 2014”), Employee Stock Option Plan 2020 (“ESOP – 2020”), Employees Stock Option Plan – 2021 (“ESOP – 2021”) and Employee Stock Option Plan 2024 (“ESOP– 2024”). With an objective to implement the ESOP– 2014 and ESOP– 2020, the Company formed the Etechaces Employees Stock Option Plan Trust (the “ESOP Trust”) to hold or possess Equity Shares and subsequently allot or transfer them to employees in accordance with the terms of the ESOP Schemes, as applicable. ESOP – 2021 and ESOP – 2024 schemes are implemented and administered directly by the Company.
For Grant 24, the fair value at grant date is determined using the Black-Scholes-Merton model and Monte-Carlo Simulations methodology. The model takes into account the exercise price, the term of the option, the share price at grant date and expected price volatility of the underlying share, the expected dividend yield, the risk free interest rate for the term of the option and probability of satisfying market linked condition of share price.

For Grant 25, the fair value at grant date is determined using the Black-Scholes-Merton model. The model takes into account the exercise price, the term of the option, the share price at grant date and expected price volatility of the underlying share, the expected dividend yield and the risk free interest rate for the term of the option.

Management: Good evening, everyone, and a very warm welcome to PB Fintech Limited Earnings Conference Call Q2FY27. Thank you for joining us today. On the call today, we have:
• Mr. Yashish Dahiya, Chairman & Group CEO, PB Fintech • Mr. Alok Bansal, Executive Vice Chairman, PB Fintech • Mr. Sarbvir Singh, Joint Group CEO, PB Fintech • Ms. Santosh Agarwal, CEO, Paisabazaar • Mr. Dhruv Sarin, CEO, PB Partners • Mr. Mandeep Mehta, Group CFO, PB Fintech, and • Mr. Mohit Khobragade, Head, Investor Relations, PB Fintech

chunks.section: Nov 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Earnings Call
chunks.text:
We will begin with opening remarks from the management, followed by Q&A session. I now invite Yashish to share his opening remarks. Over to you, Yashish.
Management: Thank you, Mohit. Good afternoon, good evening, good morning to everyone, wherever you are joining from. Thank you for joining us. We've had another strong quarter with healthy growth across insurance and credit. The total insurance premium for the quarter was ₹9,385 Cr, up 38% year-on-year, setting us up well for over ₹40,000 Cr this year. As always, growth was led by protection, because that's our focus from day one, and continues to be our focus. Core online new health and term grew 42% YoY, and within this, new health grew 46% YoY. Consolidated operating revenue grew 35% to ₹2,178 Cr. Core insurance revenue was up 42% YoY and core credit revenue, up 19% YoY. PAT grew 43% to ₹192 Cr, and PAT margin improved from 8% to 9%. The quality of this growth shows in its consistency. Core new premium, excluding savings, has now grown at above 34% for 14 consecutive quarters. And our core renewal and trail revenue is now over ₹1,000 Cr, it's almost ₹1,100 Cr. On a rolling 12-month basis, up 42% year-on-year. In credit, disbursals grew 22% in the core business and this has now risen for 5 consecutive quarters. Our insurance-led new initiatives, PB Partners, UAE Business, and PB for Business, delivered ₹826 Cr of revenue, up 40% and are now close to break-even. UAE Premium grew 36% YoY.

chunks.section: Nov 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Earnings Call
chunks.text: Let me now address the question straight up, which I'm assuming is on everybody's mind. First of all, where do we stand on IRDAI's consultation paper? IRDAI's consultation paper aims for lower mis-selling, better claims experience, lower prices, and deeper penetration. We absolutely support all of these goals fully. These are the goals Policybazaar was built on. Our first campaign back in 2009 was ‘Ullu Mat Bano’, aimed at addressing mis-selling. We have engaged constructively with the regulator, and we will implement the final framework fully, and in its spirit. Second, the impact. Lower distribution payouts will reduce our insurance distribution revenue, for sure. We are working on three fronts. We will expand our non-insurance revenue within and as the regulator permits and there is some anticipation that could happen. In the discussion paper, it does mention that. We will accelerate our ecosystem offerings. And as any long-term business should, we are evaluating other options to strengthen our business over time. We will share much more on this as and when the time is appropriate. Now, why do we remain confident? Health and term insurance stay deeply under-penetrated. And for the consumer, it's not really about buying the policy. The customer gets nothing on the day he buys it. The real test comes at claims. And I would like to just cover our record. On the four points that the regulators themselves lay out. On claims in the health insurance industry, the industry data says 87% of health claims are settled. That same number for Policybazaar customers is 97%. Last year, 11,156 rejected claims worth ₹185 Cr were reopened after initial rejection and paid. In the first half of this year alone, we supported about 1.25 lakh health claims and 80,000 motor claims. Our customer satisfaction is consistently above 90%.

chunks.section: Nov 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Earnings Call
chunks.text:
On persistency, 71% of our life policies are still in force at month 61. This is against a benchmark of 51% to 66% for the large players. Our renewal in health insurance is at 89%, rising to 91% from second-year renewals onwards. On mis-selling, in the life insurance category, we get 16 complaints from our customers per 10,000 customers. This is against a benchmark of 30 to 53. In health insurance, we get 21 claim complaints for every 10,000 claims. This is against a benchmark of 29 to 54. On

price reduction, for the plans they choose, our health customers pay, on average, 9% less and up to 30% less than some other channels. And on reach and expansion of the market, about 40% of new customers added in Retail Health across the country come through us. More than a quarter of India's pure term premium, 17.8% of the retail health premium came through us last year. 74% of our term policies and 64% of our health policies come from Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities. These outcomes are very much required in the country and that is why we, as a management team, are super confident that we solve this particular problem. We are a part of the solution, and we will only grow stronger through this. Our credit business and our UAE business are growing, and outside this broad framework. We will maintain strict cost discipline over the years as we go through this period. What will we not do? While maintaining this cost discipline, and profitability focus, we will not cut back on the customer proposition. Not one step back on that. Choice, transparency, and claim support remain non-negotiable. We will remain fully compliant and consult with the regulator on whatever we do in this area. Finally, since our listing, quarterly revenue has grown from ₹280 Cr to ₹2,178 Cr, a 51% CAGR, and the PAT margin has moved from -73% to 9%. That came from building around what customers need. And we have a very clear, let's call it, mission, or strategy, whatever you want to call it. Over the next 1000 days, we will serve customers well, we will stay focused on that, we will stay disciplined on cost, and we will keep investing in a market that remains deeply underpenetrated. It's a very simple strategy. Thank you. Look forward to your questions.

Management: Thank you, Yashish. We will now move to the Q&A session.
Management: We will take the first question from the line of Sachin Salgaonkar from BofA. Sachin, please unmute your mic.
Sachin Salgaonkar: Hi Mohit, thank you. Good day, management. I have 3 questions. First question, want to understand anything specific happened in the quarter which led to an increase in selling and marketing expenses and other expenses, both in terms of QoQ as well as YoY.
Management: Sachin, two things have happened. Last year, because of the GST impact and everything, and I think it was kind of pre-GST, although this quarter. But somehow, last year, from June to, obviously till December, the demand was very robust, and which meant that we spent, I would say, lower than our normal level of spending in marketing. This year, it's been the reverse. Actually, demand has been very tough, and I think we've had to spend a lot more money. So I would say that if you look at it on a two-year basis, you'll find it's not that dramatic. But yeah, versus last year, it will look as if it was higher. And it was just lack of demand in the market, and I think we had to spend money to make sure that we got the leads.

Sachin Salgaonkar: Got it. And, to follow up on this, how should we think about the incremental spending in next, let's say, 3 to 6 months? And I'm asking from a point of view that there is this entire overhang associated in terms of these commission structure gets implemented. Is there a school of thought that it would make sense to control costs, particularly the discretionary items, and show contribution margin improvement. In the opening remark, Yashish did mention about being disciplined from a cost point of view. And how do you look to sort of, balance it in context of what you indicated, that from a demand point of view, things are a bit tough in the near term?

And we could have been a little aggressive on cost, because that was not the highest priority. Now, that does not imply we were wasteful. As we move forward, the cost consciousness will be there, but that does not mean we are backing off from growth. I think growth stays very critical in this market. Two things. First of all, the market needs it. And I think in a way, scale is very important. And thus, we are going to keep

Management: Hi guys, thank you for joining the call. We started this company in 2008 with a very clear objective to improve Social Security in the country. And in Social Security, the primary products were Term and Health. Within that, term insurance, when we started, used to have a commission of 0. And, health insurance was the same as motor insurance. So the primary reason we built these businesses was because we felt these were important products for the Indian middle class. Secondly, we've had some regulatory updates last evening and, we just wanted to clarify that we do a little more than a broker. We spend a lot of money in advertising and marketing to build awareness for the category. We do a lot of underwriting and risk management, because of which insurers get better quality business. We, of course, do distribution. But we also outdo what a distributor would usually do, in terms of customer service and claim support. We manage, for example, our own networks of garages, PB garages. We have a network of hospitals called PB Care+. We also have an investment in PB Health, which is a chain of hospitals. We also have a reinsurance brokerage. I just wanted to say these are additional activities from what you would find from a normal broker. In terms of our revenue lines, we have two clear revenue lines. One is life insurance, the second is general insurance. From the current regulations, in terms of net present value, we think the life insurance net present value is similar to what we have today, and should not have a major impact. But in terms of general insurance, it is between one-third to 40% of what we have today. That's a very serious impact on revenue. And we are thinking about what the implications of that are. We do have cost rationalization opportunities.

chunks.section: Sep 2026 earnings call · Q1 FY2027 · PB FINTECH LIMITED
chunks.text: And those would be in terms of how much we spend on digital marketing, how aggressive we are there, how aggressive we are in terms of brand spend. And also how aggressive we might be in terms of sales and customer support. Historically, our effort has been to be aggressive to drive growth for the overall industry. However, given the new economics, there may be opportunities for rationalization there, and we will look at that. With most of our general insurance partners, we work on a combined operating ratio model. What that implies is, if any component of the combined operating ratio, whether it is claims ratio or whether it is commissions, they come down, from whatever was the ongoing, that can reflect itself in terms of consumer pricing. And thus, you can see higher volumes because of more aggressive consumer pricing. Also, in term of service, we not just do marketing, consulting, technology, administration of policies, but we also manage networks. So, there is also possibility of us working with our partners for getting service revenues for these activities, including reinsurance support, because as you can imagine, we are not just a distributor, we are also a risk manager. So, and we are also exploring all options in terms of manufacturing, whether that be insurance or reinsurance, so we will explore those, we're at early stages of exploration of that. I don't know if Sarbvir or Alok, you want to add anything at this stage, otherwise, we can open it up to questions.

See, today, for selling a fresh health insurance policy, an agent was being paid, give or take, ₹15,000. That is actually what an agent was being paid in the market. If these regulations are to be implemented exactly as they are being said, that same agent selling a health insurance policy is going to get ₹3,500 to ₹3,750. For somebody who was earning ₹15,000 selling 2 policies a month, suddenly getting ₹3,750 even if he manages to sell 3 policies a month, I don't know if that is rewarding enough. chunks.section: Sep 2026 earnings call · Q1 FY2027 · PB FINTECH LIMITED
chunks.text: actually, the person will still probably earn ₹15,000, because they would be taken on the roll of the company. So, I think some of the impact will be nullified that way. So, we have to actually focus on and improve that, if we want the industry to go better. If distribution was the engine that was pushing the sales, I think taking the engine out of the car and making it lighter will not make the car go faster, is my opinion. I could be wrong in that. And I think most industry will figure out. As I said, in agents, they might find a way to give the people a salary, there may be some arrangement for banks, people will figure out their arrangement, I believe. Earnings Call
August 05, 2026
Management: Hello everyone. A very good evening and a very warm welcome to PB Fintech Limited Earnings Conference Call for Q1 FY27. Today, we have with us:
• Mr. Yashish Dahiya, Chairman & Group CEO, PB Fintech • Mr. Alok Bansal, Executive Vice Chairman, PB Fintech • Mr. Sarbvir Singh, Joint Group CEO, PB Fintech • Ms. Santosh Agarwal, CEO, Paisabazaar • Mr. Mandeep Mehta, Group CFO, PB Fintech, and • Mr. Mohit Khobragade, Head, Investor Relations, PB Fintech
I now request Yashish for his introductory note.
Management: Thanks, Mohit.
Good evening everybody and thank you for joining us. We've started FY27 on a strong note, with healthy growth across most of our insurance and credit businesses, actually all. The overall insurance premium, is now at ₹8,372 Cr, it's grown at 41% year-on-year. Importantly, this growth continues to be led by the protection categories, which is our focus. New health and term insurance grew at 53%, with new health growing at 59% year-on-year, for the core business. This is an important indicator of both the opportunity in the market and the strength of our platform. Health and term both remain significantly under-penetrated as categories, and for our large and growing middle class, social security is very critical. That's sort of our big problem to solve.

chunks.section: Aug 2026 earnings call · Q1 FY2027 · Earnings Call
chunks.text:
Our consolidated operating revenue grew 40% to ₹1,888 Cr, with core insurance revenue growing at 46% and core credit revenue growing at 25% year-on-year. The consolidated PAT increased 92% year-on-year, (which is, again, both going to the new business as well as the renewal business), to ₹163 Cr, while PAT margin improved from 6% to 9% year-on-year. Just to put it in perspective, that also means, for the last 12 months, our PAT would be just about ₹750 Cr +/-, right now. So, starting to kind of inch towards our target number for the year.
Our core online total premium grew 41% year-on-year, for the quarter. Core new insurance premium, including savings, grew at 39%, excluding savings is 48% YoY growth. This is amongst the highest we've ever had. If you remember, for the last 13 quarters now, we have been upwards of 35% for our total new premium growth, excluding savings. The quality of the growth is also visible in our renewal and trail revenue. While our renewal revenue has grown at 55% to ₹1,003 Cr for the last 12 months, but now we're getting to a stage when you will see higher and higher growth in renewals, because this is the previous 3 years of fresh growth starting to pay off. So you will see higher and higher numbers in renewal growth, here onwards.

chunks.section: Aug 2026 earnings call · Q1 FY2027 · Earnings Call
chunks.text:
Building trust beyond the point of sale is important. Insurance is clearly not about just helping customers buy a policy. Actually, the customer gets nothing when he buys a policy. The real test comes when they use that policy, which is at the point of claims. Basically, both in getting the policy, as well as in claims. We now are at above 90% in terms of CSAT. We have supported ~70,000 claims in this quarter that just went by, for health insurance. We are increasingly using technology and claim-related information to make customers' conversations more transparent. Our advisors can demonstrate real-time, real claims outcomes. So, when a customer comes to us, we're able to explain to the customer in and around their area, how many claims we have settled. And should the customer be willing, we can even connect them to those customers for referral calls, etc. All this is very powerful in convincing new customers to buy from us. And this is being done at scale using tech.
In our credit business, the core revenue grew 25%, while, as I said, the core disbursals grew 33%. So the good news is credit is also back into growth now. The total credit disbursal is now at ₹4,366 Cr for the quarter. The business continues to focus on customers with all different credit profiles. If you really think about it, there is a

high-end customer, there's a middle-end customer, and there is a customer who cannot really get credit. We are helping all three, we solve their problems, and all three obviously have very different problems.

high-end customer, there's a middle-end customer, and there is a customer who cannot really get credit. We are helping all three, we solve their problems, and all three obviously have very different problems.
PB Partners is expanding, clearly, across all areas. Now, 78% of the GWP comes from Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities. We now have more than 500,000 advisors, with the active partner count increasing 55% year-on-year to 1.13 lacs for this quarter that's gone by. Our strategy has been to increasingly work with smaller, higher quality advisors, and equip them with technology, product access, training, and service support. We, of course, cover 99% of India's PIN codes, more than 19,000 PIN codes. Our quarterly premium grew 46% year-on-year to ₹1,637 Cr, while revenue grew 47% to ₹561 Cr. A few data points which we are starting to share now. The share of employee benefit expenses was about 15% of the revenue for the quarter. It was 12% in the previous quarter, but that is because it was seasonally a bigger quarter, but it's 15% of revenue right now. Our top 100 partners' share of premium is 16%. We will further work actively in reducing this. We are very good in this; once we track something, we really get it sorted. But it is 16% right now. We believe PB Partners can play an important role in increasing insurance access across India by combining local relationships with Policybazaar’s technology, product breadth and service capabilities.

chunks.section: Aug 2026 earnings call · Q1 FY2027 · Earnings Call
chunks.text:
Now, this actually has quite astounded me, because I don't think anybody expects this. Because there's a lot going on in the UAE, but growth is not one of those things. Our UAE insurance premium grew 31% year-on-year for this quarter. Most of what we do is health and life insurance, similar to evolution of our India business. Again, cross-border is a big part, so people who retire, need health insurance in India, people need to plan for their children's education, etc. So that business has done well and has been very resilient in tough times. Our new initiatives continue to scale forward across the board.
To conclude, we are seeing strong momentum across the group. As you know, insurance premium grew 41%, revenue grew 40%, PAT grew 92%, PAT margin improved to 9%. The interesting part is to look at this over time. Over the last 5 years, from Q1FY22 to Q1FY27, our quarterly revenue has grown from ₹238 Cr to ₹1,888 Cr, which is a CAGR of 51%. Some quarters, something has worked, some quarters, something else has worked, but overall, CAGR of our growth has been 51% over a 5-year period, which is quite astounding. At the same time, our PAT margin has improved from -47% to 9%, and for those of us who track financial numbers better than I do, the best is just starting to come. So, thank you, and I'll start looking forward to questions.

I think it works when you put these three things together. Increasingly we get emails from people saying – Please port my policy to Policybazaar; I have not bought from you, but I want to use your services. And I think that is an indication of the kind of the work that has been going on. And I feel that it's still early days. I think there is a lot more to go, and I think we can continue to grow faster than the market. What the level will be, time will tell. chunks.section: Aug 2026 earnings call · Q1 FY2027 · Earnings Call
chunks.text: I also want to give you one or two examples of things that I think Policybazaar does, which many others don't want to do. One is, like, the use of monthly mode. So, if you see, in health insurance, largely, I think we are the only platform that really sells any scale on monthly mode. And almost over 30% of our business now comes on monthly mode. We collect all those monthly payments, we ensure persistency, we ensure renewal, and that's an investment. I mean, you have to put in the investment to do all these things. But I think there's a lot of discussion about missing middle, affordable products. This makes the product affordable, it allows people who are not very high income to get things. Similarly, I’ll just explain another product that we've been doing for a while, which is maternity. Typically, maternity has, like, a 1-year or a 2-year waiting period. We have a product where we are offering 3-month waiting period. Now, there's a structure over there, but this gives a lot of young families a reason to buy health insurance, and then, of course, they stay, and then they renew. Now, again, this is a little bit of investment upfront into something that pays off. I think these are the two things we take a long-term view. We look at customer acquisition on a lifetime value basis. And number two, as I said, we have really worked on the three things that matter. Bringing traffic; good products and then offering very high level of service and claim support.

chunks.section: Aug 2026 earnings call · Q1 FY2027 · Earnings Call
chunks.text: Management: Yeah, I would say don't even think about the worst-case scenario. Let me come to the very basic thing. Legally, as defined by the regulator, the largest amount of effort in any sale needs to be put by a broker, more than any other channel. And that is as legally defined, in terms of tasks to be undertaken, by the regulator. In terms of customer support, in terms of sales, in terms of claims support, in terms of everything. So it's a very difficult position to take that the entity that is supposed to put the maximum effort is somehow meant to do the less effort. So, these things are legal at the end of it, and I would kind of leave it there. I think there's been way too many statements and way too many things, and I'm sure wisdom is developing. I use that word very carefully. And I think it'll develop more. And I think we will see the result of it as it happens. I don't anticipate anything. Sometimes when you do these media interviews, it's very strange, and that's why I stopped doing media interviews, thankfully. I wasn't very pleased about doing them in the first place, but sometimes, you come under pressure and you do them because your own PR team is saying you need to do them, etc, etc. Now what actually happens is, you say 10 things. And one of those things is the one they pick up, and that thing you said at point number 9, and they make it the headline. And look, that's the reason, I guess, a lot of people in the regulated industry don't do interviews. It doesn't make any sense here. You're just kind of exaggerating something which is a side point.

chunks.text: Management: First of all, I want to make it clear that none of us want to say anything about the regulator. I think that is an independent process, and, we have nothing to do with it. I think the point I just want to explain, Sachin to you and everyone on the call, is that, we've had two instances in the last five years. I've only been in this business for a short time. Where we have seen that; you had COVID, you had a great run, increase in demand for health and term insurance. The minute COVID finished, and it was like the mother of all epidemics the world has ever seen, it was across the world; immediately, the demand went away. Right now, we are in the middle of this GST thing. We saw Q3, very big; Q4, big. Now in Q1, it has already started to fade, and I think we'll be lucky if it goes through in Q2. So, the point I'm trying to make is that demand for insurance is extremely low. So, anyone who's selling insurance, by definition, has to make a significant effort to get there, and I think for a platform like ours, that effort is very, very visible in terms of the marketing spend that we have to do, the conversion, the resources that we have to deploy, the focus on service and claims. I just want to just put out that this is the level of effort that is required. So it's not easy. I mean, the trend doesn't last more than even two quarters, really.

See, we spent the last two-three months just thinking a little harder about various data points, etc, and one of the interesting pieces that we came out with was that when you look at health insurance data over the last 10 years that we have had, customers who joined us 10 years ago, and we explore that data more deeply. Only 5% of these lives; so, if 100 customers bought insurance 10 years ago, only 5 of them used a claim more than once. Another about 8 or 10 use the claim once and the rest never claimed for 10 years. And I won't take a long time. The remaining 85-odd customers that you're talking about and that represents about 67% of all insurance policies, have no customer who has ever claimed for the last 10 years, and have been paying premiums for a 10-year period. Those 67 do not interact with anybody. And usually, the one who's responsible for bringing these customers into the insurance fold is some kind of mandation. So, if you look across the insurance industry, you will usually find customers buy products when they are mandated. But otherwise, it's a very difficult job to bring this 67% of policies into the insurance fold to pay premiums year on year without claiming for a single year over a 10-year period. And this is the job that is entrusted to the insurance industry. And I think this is the part, every time somebody wakes up in the morning and tries to compare health insurance and term insurance with any other product like a mutual fund, or even the insurance savings products, etc, I think they make this mistake that this 67% actually is not going to claim at all.

Because even over a 10-year period, their claims ratio at a life level is almost 700-800%. At a policy level, it is about 300%, so they cannot afford these policies. Management: Supratim, as you can imagine, the customers are roughly the same, but what has changed is the fact that, one, there was a lot of exposure to people about term insurance and health insurance, because there was a lot of discussion during the GST time. However, what has happened post-GST is that in health insurance, for instance, people are buying higher sum insured than they were buying earlier. So, if you look at the proportion of policies below ₹10 lakhs and greater than ₹10 lakhs, now a vast majority of policies are being bought which are ₹10 lakhs and above in terms of sum insured. So that has pushed up the ticket size somewhat, and that is helping. There have also been a couple of insurers who have launched unlimited sum-insured products, their pricing is around ₹25 lakh sum- insured type range. So, those also have helped, because now people are attracted by the fact that they can have unlimited sum insurance. So, I think that is what has changed to some extent on the health side. On the term side, the change has been, again, because the customer is seeing a 18% reduction, because, prices have not changed on both health and term insurance. And what that has led to is that people are buying; there the sum assured hasn't gone up by that much, because, people tend to think in bigger buckets, like, you think of ₹1 Cr, then ₹2 Cr etc. But people have been buying a little bit more of the riders. So, things like a critical illness rider, the attachment of that has gone up; some of the accidental protection riders, their attachment has gone up. So, I think that has changed post-September, but both of these changes are dwarfed by a different change, which is the fact that our conversion rate has gone up. So, for the people who are coming, more of them are buying, because I guess they are a little bit more aware about the value of insurance.

chunks.section: May 2026 earnings call · Q4 FY2026 · Manas Agrawal: Got it. Thank you.
chunks.text: Management: Avoiding the use of the term J-curve, I would say that, savings for insurance, we have to figure out what is the customer proposition, because, see, total amount of savings, we can see the growth in SIP, we can see the growth in mutual funds, etc, bonds, everything. So, it's not that the total amount of savings in the country is a challenge, I think the savings coming to insurance is definitely, to some extent, you can argue, is a challenge. And I think the main thing is the customer proposition. And one of the things that we have always tried to do is to start from the customer, rather than starting from what we want to sell. Many years ago, when Santosh was leading the business, she introduced the concept of a capital guarantee, where we said that your premium will be guaranteed, we will ensure that we get your premium back, and then you have upside in terms of the market. That was an innovation that did well. Now we are trying to go to the next level, where we are saying that the reason you should invest in a ULIP is that you at least have to be in the product for 5 years, that's the base term of the product. Obviously, you can stay 10, 15, 20 years. And we're saying that the reason is that you tie a goal to the investment. It's not a frivolous thing that, okay, let me put some money into the market and see because there's a war going on, or whatever. It's a goal that you have. One goal, it could be child education, could be buying a house, could be your retirement. So, these goals are serious goals for which you have to remain invested. That's what a ULIP really does well. Second, ULIPs have a feature which is called waiver of premium, which means that should something happen to you, the insurance company will continue to pay your premiums, also pay out the sum assured, give a monthly income to your family.

chunks.section: May 2026 earnings call · Q4 FY2026 · Manas Agrawal: Got it. Thank you.
chunks.text: Here, you have not just planned for the goal, but you have protected the goal. And then the third thing is that still ULIPs enjoy a tax advantage up to ₹2.5 lakhs, so they are actually, right now, the best investment. And within that ₹2.5 lakhs tax advantage, you also have the ability to switch from equity to debt. So, it's the only debt product available in the country without having to pay tax on it. So, there are 3 very big advantages of ULIPs. I think we are going to promote this more and more. This is something that we have been doing even earlier, but we are going to promote these things more, and we believe that this will attract customers for the right reasons. See, many times we forget that despite all the discussion about SIPs and mutual funds, after 5 years, the number of active SIPs, the estimates vary from 3% to 11% or something. So, after 5 years in our ULIP, the persistency is somewhere in the 70-75% range. So, the customer that we are getting is a good customer. I think we just need to talk more about the advantages, and it's not for me to say what the industry should do or not do, but I do believe that all of us have to start from the customer and offer a proposition which is good for the customer. Waiver of premium is a great proposition.

chunks.text: Management: And Prayesh, if you look at the data, and I'll just take one minute on this. I think as we look at the next 5 years or so, what we have to do is to give something back to the non-claimers also. Whether that comes in terms of maternity cover, whether that comes in terms of some gym access, some wellness benefits, OPD benefits, etc, somewhere we have to sweeten the deal for them, because right now, they're getting nothing. So young people, etc, coming in are getting nothing. And as we talk about the people who are regular claimers, we have to bring them into participation. And please understand, right now, participation is hated as a word, but participation can be in terms of co-pay, can be in terms of limited networks, can be in terms of tiered networks, various things. But without this participation, please appreciate the cost is going to become unsustainable for the industry; we're not doing this out of joy, we're doing this out of necessity. The cost will become unsustainable for the industry. So those are the two things that we have to work on, make it better for the people who do not claim, so that more and more of them come and get something out of it, and bring participation from the regular claimers, because without that, it won't be sustainable and they're very few to work on.
